name: Vector Equities
tagline: 500 public companies rendered as 4,831 company-years of SEC EDGAR XBRL and market data, embedded into 64 dimensions covering fiscal 2015 through 2024.

headline_stats.label: recall@10 on the 500 held-out test pairs
sector purity@10 lift over random (0.7057 vs 0.1117)
input features with zero coverage - dead in the trained model

insights.title: The sector clustering is mostly the same company standing next to itself
insights.body: Nearest-neighbor sector purity@10 reads 0.7057 against a random-assignment baseline of 0.1117 - a 6.32x lift. But when neighbors drawn from the query row's own ticker are excluded, purity falls to 0.4013 (3.59x lift), and the cosine silhouette score of the sector clusters is -0.0034, versus -0.0204 for randomly permuted labels. Most of the headline coherence is a company's own ten fiscal years sitting on top of each other, which contrastive training guarantees by construction.

insights.title: Three towers are feeding the model nothing at all
insights.body: The feature audit flags 33 of 118 features at 0.0 coverage: all 6 ownership features (INST_PCT, SHORT_INTEREST_PCT, INSIDER_NET_12M, FLOAT_PCT, TOP10_INST_CONC, INST_DELTA_QOQ), all 6 disclosure_text features (MDA_SENTIMENT, RISK_FACTOR_COUNT, FOG_INDEX_PROXY among them), all 3 sector_context features, and 12 of the 14 management_neo features including CEO_TENURE and BOARD_INDEP_PCT. It shows in the outputs: the Management_Quality skill spans only 0.3312 to 0.6575 across all 4,831 rows and Disclosure_Quality only 0.3449 to 0.6437, while Balance_Health - fed by live XBRL - spans -0.0445 to 1.2711.
insights.source: pipeline/data/feature_audit.json -> dead_or_constant; assets/real_data.json -> points[].skills, indices for Management_Quality / Disclosure_Quality / Balance_Health

insights.title: The archetype head calls JPMorgan a SaaS company
insights.body: Cross-cycle archetype purity@20 is 0.4855 and sector top-1 accuracy is 0.5454 over the 8 of 11 sectors that were scored at all (see the label-mismatch insight below), and the labels show why. HyperGrowth_SaaS absorbs 1,984 of 4,831 rows (41.1%), including JPMorgan in 9 of its 10 years, Bank of America in 9 of 10, Southern Company in 2017 and Starbucks in 2024. Meanwhile Microsoft's 2022 row is labeled Bank_Capital_Heavy and Nucor's 2022 row is labeled Moonshot_Bio. The Turnaround archetype gets 137 rows in total.
insights.source: assets/real_data.json -> points[].archetype (counts by label and by ticker); pipeline/data/mtnn_report.json -> cross_cycle_archetype_purity_at_20, sector_top1_acc

insights.title: The forward head is calibrated, and the calibration does not count
insights.body: The isotonic fit takes the forward drawdown head's predicted mean from 0.1137 down to 0.0561 against a true mean of 0.0561 - bias_after 0.0, inside the stated <1.0% tolerance, with IC nudged from 0.87843 to 0.88106. The artifact still records passed: false, because passed_requires is 'bias_within_tolerance AND trained_on == real' and trained_on is 'synthetic matching 11.37% vs 5.61% spec + real bundle if available'. An IC of 0.88106 against a stated ic_target of 0.5066 is itself a signal the fit is not seeing real out-of-sample data.
insights.source: assets/forward_calibration_isotonic.json -> passed, passed_requires, trained_on, pred_mean_before, pred_mean_after, bias_after, ic_after, ic_target

insights.title: Next-year prediction is weak, and the model's own report says so
insights.body: The next_profile head explains 26.2% of variance on validation (r2 0.262, MAE 0.2516 z) and 19.65% on the 500 test rows (r2 0.1965, RMSE 0.6511). Market directional accuracy is 0.6581. Those roll into a composite quality score of 0.6154 that cleared the promote gate on the strength of retrieval rather than forecasting - inside composite.parts, recall contributes 0.91 while r2_clip contributes 0.1965.
insights.source: pipeline/data/mtnn_report.json -> next_profile.val, next_profile.test, market_directional_acc, composite.parts, promote.reason

insights.title: That sector number was an 8-class problem wearing an 11-class name
insights.body: feature_spec.SECTORS spells the GICS sectors with underscores. The training matrix spells them with spaces. The lookup fell back to -1, so Consumer Discretionary (463 rows), Consumer Staples (328) and Real Estate (307) — 1,098 of 4,831, 22.7% of the corpus — were never assigned a sector at all. The loss masks -1 and so does the accuracy metric, so nothing crashed and nothing looked wrong: 0.5454 was computed over 3,733 rows and 8 classes. The real damage was elsewhere. The contrastive loss boosts hard negatives for any pair sharing a sector label, and it does NOT mask -1, so those three sectors were trained as a single merged pseudo-sector. Fixing the mapping and re-running five paired seeds moves sector accuracy from 0.5697 to 0.5058 — an 11-class problem over every company is harder than an 8-class one over 77% of them — while retrieval, purity and next-year R2 stay flat. The drop is the measurement becoming honest, not the model getting worse.
insights.source: vector-equities/pipeline/data/ab_sector_labels.json -> rows_unmapped=1098, rows_total=4831, pct_unmapped=22.7, classes_scored_buggy=8, classes_scored_fixed=11, rows_scored_buggy=3733, sector_acc_buggy=0.5697, sector_acc_fixed=0.5058, n_seeds=5; pipeline/data/mtnn_report.json -> sector_top1_acc=0.5454

game.prompt: Two real company-years from the model's training set. Which one does Vector Equities score higher on Balance_Health?
game.explainer: Balance_Health is one of 12 skill-head outputs the MTNN predicts from a company-year's SEC XBRL feature vector; across all 4,831 rows it averages 0.4905 and runs from -0.0445 (Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings, 2024) to 1.2711 (Fastenal, 2019), so a higher number means the model reads that year's balance sheet as further from distress.

rounds.reveal: Same fiscal year, opposite trajectories: Tesla climbs from 0.2360 in 2016 to 0.7094 in 2023 (81.5th percentile of all 4,831 rows) while Boeing falls from 0.4458 in 2016 to a low of 0.1688 in 2021 and recovers only to 0.2755 (18.1st percentile).

The closest call on the board - 0.0016 apart, at the 0.9th and 1.0th percentiles. Starbucks 2024 is its own ten-year low, down from 0.3077 in 2015; Marriott has lived in this basement the whole decade, never above 0.1703 and dipping to -0.0033 in 2019.

A regulated utility scores below a cruise line in the year cruising stopped. Southern's 2017 row sits at the 0th percentile of all 4,831 rows and the company posts negative Balance_Health in four separate years (-0.0415, -0.0147, -0.0161, -0.0161); Royal Caribbean's 2020 row is 0.0365, though it does go negative later, bottoming at -0.0360 in 2024.

3M drops from 0.7615 in 2022 to 0.2257 in 2023 - a 0.5358 single-year fall, the sharpest of any name on this board - then rebounds to 0.6138 in 2024. GE runs the other way, from a 2018 trough of 0.2665 up to 0.5122.

The two curves cross in 2021. Intel slides from 0.9727 in 2015 to 0.4400 in 2024; AMD rises from 0.3236 to 0.7756 over the same span. In 2020 Intel still led 0.8545 to 0.8000; by 2021 AMD was ahead 0.8267 to 0.8030 and never gave it back.
0.0815 apart at the very top of the distribution - the 99.9th and 98.9th percentiles. Texas Instruments never drops below 1.0534 in any of its ten years; Nvidia's own decade peak is this 2018 row.
Oracle falls from 0.9212 in 2017 to 0.0616 in 2022 - the 1.5th percentile of all 4,831 rows, below cash-burning Uber at the 9.2nd. Note the model also files Uber under Industrials, not Technology.
Moderna's 2022 row is its own peak at the 97.2nd percentile, nearly double Pfizer's 0.5853 (70.1st) in the same year. Moderna does not hold it - the very next year it falls to 0.5116.

2022 is Microsoft's strongest Balance_Health year of the decade at 0.7949 (87.8th percentile), and a steel mill still beats it: Nucor posts 1.0004 at the 96.3rd. The model labels that Nucor row Moonshot_Bio and the Microsoft row Bank_Capital_Heavy.

0.0152 apart near the floor - the 3.3rd and 4.2nd percentiles. CVS falls across the decade, 0.6317 in 2015 to 0.1090 in 2024, its ten-year low; Kraft Heinz never had it, topping out at 0.1407 in 2015 and staying under 0.1450 every year since.

caveat: Recorded verbatim in the model's own eval file: "Engineering quality metric for the embedding space only; measures label coherence of the geometry, not investment merit and not predictive of returns." (assets/eval_sector_coherence.json -> note). The forward-return head backs that up - assets/forward_calibration_isotonic.json records "passed": false, because passed_requires is "bias_within_tolerance AND trained_on == 'real'" and trained_on is "synthetic matching 11.37% vs 5.61% spec + real bundle if available". Nothing here is a forecast. The sector top-1 figure on this page describes the SHIPPED model, which was trained before the sector-label mismatch was found and therefore scored on 8 of 11 sectors covering 77.3% of companies. The corrected 11-class figure on an otherwise identical config is 0.5058.
